title: Metrics That Matter: RED Dashboards, Not Vanity Numbers
objective: Instrument a service with a small, justified set of RED metrics (rate, errors, duration) and assemble them into a fixed dashboard that visibly distinguishes a healthy state from an unhealthy one.
whyThisMatters: A dashboard full of numbers nobody chose on purpose is noise. Metrics only earn their instrumentation cost if each one answers a specific operational question — the discipline this task builds is choosing (and rejecting) metrics deliberately.
evidence: A metrics justification note, including the rejected vanity-metric candidate
promtool or scrape output validating the metrics endpoint
The four PromQL queries with captured output under healthy and induced-unhealthy states
A dashboard definition file or export
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: Prometheus (or promtool check) validates the exposed metrics endpoint without errors.
The latency metric is a histogram or summary, and captured queries include p95 and p99 — not a single average.
Each of the at most six exposed metrics has a one-sentence justification tying it to a named operational question.
The dashboard/query set shows a visibly different result between the healthy and induced-unhealthy capture.
